items.prompt: An order holds 2 units at 10.00 with a 5.00 discount. The user saves, exits and restarts the delivered app. What does menu 8 show?
items.answer: Subtotal 20.00, discount 5.00, total 15.00, all as they were before
distractors: Subtotal 20.00, discount 0.00, total 20.00, as reload clamps the discount
Subtotal 20.00, discount 5.00, total 20.00, as totals are cached on save
Nothing: startup stops, as a saved discount fails the empty-order check
items.explanation: parseRows groups all item rows by order and calls Order.restore with the complete list, so the discount is checked against the full 20.00 subtotal. The regression test reloads 5.00 and 15.00. (The original app reset it to 0.)

items.prompt: An order has 3 units at 10.00 and a discount of 25.00. Menu 14 asks to change the quantity to 2. What happens?
items.answer: Refused, so quantity stays 3, discount 25.00 and total 5.00
distractors: Accepted, with the discount lowered to 20.00 and a total of 0.00
Accepted, with quantity 2 and a total of -5.00 until the next save
Accepted, with the discount cleared and a total of 20.00
items.explanation: setItemQuantity builds a candidate line and checks the proposed subtotal (20.00) against the discount before replacing anything; validateSubtotal throws "Reduce the discount before reducing the subtotal." Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: An order has moved to PAID. The user applies a new 1.00 discount with menu 10. What does the app print?
items.answer: Could not apply discount: Orders in PAID status cannot be edited.
distractors: Discount applied.
Could not apply discount: Discount cannot exceed subtotal.
Could not apply discount: Invalid order status transition from PAID.
items.explanation: applyDiscount calls ensureEditable, and isEditable is true only for DRAFT and SUBMITTED. Verified in a probe; the regression test checks the same rule for adding items.

items.prompt: A caller reads an order with service.findById, then calls getItems().get(0).setQuantity(99) on the result. What changes?
items.answer: Nothing stored, as the order and its items were both handed out as copies
distractors: The stored order, whose total grows because the item object is shared
The stored line quantity only, while the cached total stays the same
Nothing, because setQuantity throws on an item that was read from a list
items.explanation: findById returns order.copy(), and getItems maps every line through OrderItem.copy. setQuantity succeeds on that copy only. Verified in a probe (stored total still 15.00).

items.prompt: A brand-new DRAFT order has no items. In menu 11 the user chooses SUBMITTED. What does the app print?
items.answer: Could not update order status: An empty order cannot enter that status.
distractors: Order status updated.
Could not update order status: An empty order cannot be moved to SUBMITTED.
Could not update order status: Invalid status transition from DRAFT to SUBMITTED.
items.explanation: The service check for empty orders names only PAID and SHIPPED, so it passes; Order.setStatus then applies requiresItems, which includes SUBMITTED, and throws its own message. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: A SUBMITTED order has exactly one line and no discount. The user removes that line with menu 7. What happens?
items.answer: Refused, since a submitted order must keep at least one item
distractors: The line is removed and the order goes back to the DRAFT status
The line is removed, leaving an empty SUBMITTED order
Refused, since SUBMITTED orders cannot be edited at all
items.explanation: removeItemByProductId checks status == SUBMITTED && items.size() == 1 and throws "A submitted order must keep at least one item." SUBMITTED is still editable for other changes; a DRAFT order may lose its last line.

items.prompt: An order has 3 units of a 10.00 notebook. The user adds the same notebook again with quantity 1. What does the order hold?
items.answer: One notebook line of 4 units, still at its own 10.00 price snapshot
distractors: Two notebook lines, 3 units and 1 unit, each with its own price snapshot
One notebook line of 1 unit, as adding a product again replaces its line
Nothing new, as a product that is already on the order is refused
items.explanation: addOrMergeItem finds the existing productId and calls increaseQuantity on that line, keeping its captured name and unit price. Verified in a probe (1 line, qty 4, unit 10.00).

items.prompt: In menu 3 the user enters 0.004 as a product price. What does the app print?
items.answer: Please enter a non-negative amount with at most 2 decimal places, for example 19.99.
distractors: Could not create product: Money must be greater than zero.
Created product with ID ... (stored at 0.00 after rounding the price)
Created product with ID ... (stored at 0.01 after rounding the price up)
items.explanation: readMoney passes the parsed value to DomainValues.money, whose setScale(2, UNNECESSARY) throws; readMoney catches it, prints its own hint and returns null, so the flow stops. Verified with piped input.

items.prompt: Why does FileDataStore rebuild orders with Order.restore instead of creating a DRAFT and replaying addOrMergeItem and setStatus?
items.answer: Replay runs the user-command rules and stamps a new updatedAt; restore avoids both
distractors: Replaying would be correct but slow, as each call recalculates every total
addOrMergeItem cannot add lines whose product is not in the catalog yet
restore skips validation entirely, so damaged files can still be repaired
items.explanation: 02-CONCEPTS: restoration is not applying user commands. Replaying addOrMergeItem on a loaded order goes through the edit rules (ensureEditable) and touch(), so a saved non-editable order or its update time would not come back as saved. restore builds the complete aggregate and validates it directly.

items.prompt: Startup finds a snapshot whose footer counts are wrong. What does the app do, and with which process exit status?
items.answer: It prints the Startup stopped message and reason, then exits with status 0
distractors: It prints the reason, then calls System.exit(1) so scripts see a failure
Starts with empty data and overwrites the snapshot on the next save
Falls back to the four legacy files, if they still exist, and continues
items.explanation: main catches the RuntimeException from load, prints "Startup stopped: ..." and "Existing data was not replaced..." and returns, so the JVM exits 0. Verified on data/sample-corrupt.

items.prompt: There is no oms.snapshot.txt, and the directory holds customers.txt, products.txt and orders.txt but no order_items.txt. What does load do?
items.answer: Fails with "Incomplete legacy dataset: all four files are required."
distractors: Loads the orders with no items, then writes a fresh snapshot on the next save
Ignores the three files and starts with an empty dataset
Loads the three files and creates order_items.txt on the next save
items.explanation: The loader counts how many of the four legacy files exist and refuses any count other than 0 or 4. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: The user chooses 13 (Exit), but the save fails because the data directory is read-only. What happens next?
items.answer: It reports the failure and keeps the session open for a retry
distractors: It reports the failure and exits, dropping the unsaved changes
It exits normally and retries the save automatically at next start
It writes the data to a backup file beside the snapshot and exits
items.explanation: exitApplication returns true (keep running) when saveData fails and prints "Data could not be saved. Session stays open so you can retry." Reproduced by running the CLI on a data path whose parent is a file: 13 printed that line and the next menu choice was still read.

items.front: How are subtotal and total computed in the delivered Order, and why?
items.back: getSubtotal sums the current line totals and getTotal subtracts the discount. Deriving them leaves fewer facts to keep in sync; each OrderItem still keeps its own line total, maintained by its quantity method.

items.front: Give the order status transition graph.
items.back: DRAFT to SUBMITTED or CANCELLED; SUBMITTED to PAID or CANCELLED; PAID to SHIPPED or CANCELLED. SHIPPED and CANCELLED are terminal. Cancelling from PAID is a local status change only; there is no refund integration.

items.front: The aggregate, the snapshot validation and the atomic file save each protect something. What do none of them provide?
items.back: Authenticated ownership, concurrent request handling, cross-process stale-write detection, and payment idempotency. Those are the next lessons when the CLI becomes a web application.

items.front: What does the count footer in oms.snapshot.txt detect, and what does it not?
items.back: A mismatch detects ordinary truncation or missing records. It is not a checksum and does not resist intentional edits that also change the counts.

items.prompt: Before the worked change, reloading an order with two 10.00 units and a 5.00 discount showed a zero discount. What did the old loading path actually do wrong?
items.answer: It set the discount on an order with no items yet, so the clamp cut it to the zero subtotal
distractors: It parsed the discount with the wrong scale, so 5.00 was read back as 0.05 and rounded to zero
It multiplied each line before reading quantities, so the subtotal and the discount both came out zero
It wrote the discount after the items in the file, so the loader never reached the discount field
items.explanation: 03-WORKED-CHANGE lines 3-5: this was an initialization-order defect, not formatting or multiplication. The old constructor accepted the saved discount, initialized an empty item collection and immediately recalculated totals; the recalculation clamped a discount larger than the subtotal down to the subtotal, which was temporarily zero, and FileDataStore only added the items afterwards.

items.prompt: Which two refusals of saved data does the worked change describe for Order.restore, instead of a repair?
items.answer: Two lines for the same product, and a saved discount larger than the final subtotal
distractors: Two lines for the same product, which it merges, and any discount on a PAID order at all
A missing updatedAt timestamp, and a status that is not the order's latest one
A DRAFT order with no items, and any line whose price differs from the catalog
items.explanation: 03-WORKED-CHANGE line 17: the restore factory copies all item values, rejects duplicate product lines, calculates the full subtotal and validates the saved discount; a saved discount greater than the final subtotal is rejected rather than silently repaired. It preserves the saved timestamps, and paid status does not block reconstruction. A DRAFT order may hold no items; only SUBMITTED, PAID and SHIPPED orders must have lines.

items.prompt: A discount change is rejected because it has three decimal places. What happens to the order's updatedAt, and why does that matter?
items.answer: It is left unchanged, so a rejected request never looks like a successful edit
distractors: It is set to now, so that the audit trail records that someone attempted an edit
It is set to now, because every call into the aggregate counts as a touch
It is cleared to null, so the order is flagged for a later manual review
items.explanation: 03-WORKED-CHANGE line 19: changing a discount validates precision and range before assignment, and failed changes do not touch updatedAt, so a rejected request does not falsely look like a successful edit. Nothing records attempts, touches on every call, or clears the timestamp.

items.prompt: Why did persistence move from four separately rewritten files to one snapshot file replaced atomically?
items.answer: An interruption between the four writes could combine different generations of data
distractors: Four files made every save four times slower than writing one larger snapshot file
Four files could not store the C, P, O and I tags that the new reader requires
Four files broke on Windows paths, while one snapshot file works on every system
items.explanation: 03-WORKED-CHANGE line 23: customers, products, order metadata and items used to be rewritten separately, so an interruption could combine different generations of data. The new save validates and serializes a complete snapshot, writes a temporary sibling and atomically replaces the destination. Speed, tags and path handling are not the stated reason.

items.prompt: The C# entity sketch adds one property the Java Order lacks and computes Total with no clamp. What is added, and why is the clamp unnecessary?
items.answer: A [ConcurrencyCheck] Version; ApplyDiscount already refuses a discount above Subtotal
distractors: A RowVersion byte array; the database rejects a negative Total with a CHECK constraint
A [Timestamp] UpdatedAt; Total is rounded to zero by EF whenever it would go negative
A [Required] CustomerId; Subtotal always exceeds any discount because of the line prices
items.explanation: 08-C# lines 18-22: the sketch adds [ConcurrencyCheck] int Version, new because the Java order has no version yet (practice exercise 6), and Total is Subtotal minus DiscountAmount with no clamp, because ApplyDiscount refuses a discount larger than Subtotal, as Order.java:101 does. No CHECK constraint, EF rounding or price assumption is involved.

items.prompt: In the C# sketch, what does marking OrderItem as [Owned] say about the lines, and where does a line's UnitPrice come from?
items.answer: Lines have no identity outside their order; UnitPrice is copied at add time, never re-read
distractors: Lines are shared across orders by product; UnitPrice is read from Product on each new load
Lines get their own repository and id; UnitPrice is recomputed from the catalog nightly
Lines are stored inside the order as JSON; UnitPrice is looked up when totals are shown
items.explanation: 08-C# lines 25-31: OrderItem is [Owned], meaning it has no identity outside its order; ProductName and UnitPrice are a price snapshot copied at add time, and UnitPrice is never re-read from Product. Lines are not shared, separately repositoried or looked up later.

items.prompt: How can EF Core reproduce the Java restoration bug, and why does the OwnsMany mapping make it impossible?
items.answer: A HasMany load without Include leaves Items empty; owned types always load with the owner
distractors: A tracked load reuses stale Items from the cache; owned types are never cached by EF Core
Lazy loading fetches Items after the discount; owned types are loaded lazily in the end
A split query loads Items in a second trip; owned types are stored inside the order row
items.explanation: 08-C# lines 39-47: with a regular HasMany navigation and no Include, Items is empty, so ApplyDiscount(5m) throws against a zero subtotal (or an old-style clamp stores 0). EF Core loads owned types together with their owner on every query without Include, making OwnsMany the C# equivalent of Order.restore; separate entities need the Include inside one repository method so no caller forgets it.

items.prompt: How do the 05-PRACTICE checks exercise the app, and why does running the CLI twice against the same data copy prove a change persisted?
items.answer: Fresh JVMs on a throwaway copy of data/sample; the App saves when piped input hits EOF
distractors: One JVM reused across cases on the real data folder; each case calls the save menu last
Direct calls to OrderService on in-memory data; the second run reloads the same objects
A recorded transcript replayed against data/sample; the replay tool writes the snapshot
items.explanation: 05-PRACTICE line 3: the checks drive the real CLI in a fresh JVM against a disposable copy of data/sample. Line 13: piped input ends with EOF and the App saves on EOF, so a check that runs the CLI twice against the same copy also proves the change persisted. Nothing touches the real data, calls services directly or replays transcripts.

items.prompt: In menu 11 a user types the status teleported. What does the delivered CLI print, and what does exercise 3 ask for instead?
items.answer: A No enum constant error naming the Java class; parse explicitly and list the valid values
distractors: An Invalid menu option line; accept any word and store it as a custom status on the order
A silent switch to CANCELLED; refuse the input and keep the order in its previous status
An Unknown status line listing values; translate the message into the user's own language
items.explanation: 05-PRACTICE line 114: updateOrderStatus passes raw input to OrderStatus.valueOf, so an unknown word prints Could not update order status: No enum constant oms.domain.OrderStatus.TELEPORTED, leaking a Java class name; exercise 3 asks to parse the input explicitly and print Unknown status: ... listing the valid values. The delivered code neither stores nor silently maps the word.

items.front: The C# Order sketch: how are status, state changes, lines and money totals expressed?
items.back: enum OrderStatus { Draft, Submitted, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled }. Every property has a private setter, so state changes only through methods. Lines live in a private List<OrderItem> exposed as IReadOnlyList Items, because the aggregate root owns its lines. Subtotal is a computed property summing each line's LineTotal; nothing about the totals is stored.

items.front: Trace lab set-up: how do you start, and which records do you create before tracing?
items.back: Run the app with -DataPath pointing at a new directory (data/trace-orders). Create a customer with menu 1 (a learning address such as learner@example.test; no email is sent), an active Notebook product with menu 3 (SKU NOTE, price 10.00), and an order with menu 5 for that customer, recording each ID. IDs connect the records; names are display values, not reliable lookup keys.

items.front: Which regression tests does the worked change point you to, and where do they live?
items.back: In test/oms/RegressionTests.java: the saved-discount reload case, complete paid restoration, the failed quantity reduction, missing customer/product reference rejection, and the legacy four-file migration. The suite also covers detached copies, status guards, codec escapes, snapshot corruption and failed replacement.

items.front: What does the C# order sketch's OwnsMany configuration achieve for order lines and money columns?
items.back: Order lines are stored in their own OrderItems table, each row linked to its order through an OrderId foreign key that EF keeps as a shadow column, since OrderItem has no OrderId property. UnitPrice and DiscountAmount get HasPrecision(18, 2), so the money columns are declared with 18 digits and 2 decimal places.

items.front: Trace lab: what is the procedure for the corruption trace?
items.back: Exit, copy the learning directory to a fresh, unused destination, append a line after the count footer in the copied oms.snapshot.txt, record Get-FileHash, start the app on the copy, then record the hash again and compare. Keep the valid source directory as the recovery copy and never delete an authoritative snapshot from real learning work to force a fallback.

items.front: 05-PRACTICE: what are exercises 0 to 6, and what are the stretch steps?
items.back: 0 predict the sample orders' totals before running anything; 1 SKU uniqueness; 2 startup-failure exit behaviour; 3 status input parsing at the boundary; 4 catalog repricing with stable line snapshots (menu 15); 5 deleting DRAFT orders only (menu 16); 6 optimistic versions in the domain plus an injected Clock. Stretch (design only): an HTTP contract, transactional persistence, inventory with an outbox, and ownership on every lookup.

items.prompt: Under the C# sketch's refusal-to-HTTP table, a client first applies a 25.00 discount to an editable order whose subtotal is 20.00, then a 1.00 discount to an order whose status the guard says forbids content edits. Which statuses come back?
items.answer: 422, then 409: a broken rule, then a state conflict
distractors: 409 twice: both clash with the order's current state
422 twice: both break a domain rule of the order
400, then 404: a body error, then a missing order
items.explanation: 08-THE-SAME-ORDER-IN-CSHARP lines 53-54: a discount larger than the subtotal is a DomainException from ApplyDiscount and maps to 422, because the request is well formed but its value breaks a rule of the order. A content edit on an order whose status forbids edits is refused by the status guard and maps to 409, a conflict with the order's current state. The two refusals land on different codes, so a client can tell "fix your value" from "the order has moved on".
